action: General advice: patients should book through the channels the hospital announces while its systems are restored; health providers should keep offline backups and a plan for running appointments without digital systems.
date_note: El Dínamo (16 November) relays the hospital statement that the incident was detected on the morning of Saturday 14 November; the record earlier used 16 November, the day Emol said management reported it.
exec: A hospital's online and phone booking channels were interrupted by a cybersecurity incident, and legislators are asking whether patient records were exposed.
impact: Part of the institutional systems and the web and phone booking channels were interrupted; clinical care continued, according to the hospital.
plain: The University of Chile's Hospital Clínico in Santiago said a cybersecurity incident hit part of its systems, so appointments could not be booked online or by phone. It said care continued. Deputies asked whether patient records were exposed.
summary: The Hospital Clínico of the Universidad de Chile said a cybersecurity incident detected on the morning of Saturday 14 November interrupted part of its institutional systems, including web and phone booking, according to its statement relayed by El Dínamo. It said clinical care continued and it is working with Chile's National Cybersecurity Agency (ANCI). Deputies filed five oversight requests asking whether patient records were compromised, Emol reports; neither article says whether data was accessed.
title: Chile's Hospital Clínico de la Universidad de Chile reports cybersecurity incident; booking channels down

validation.note: El Dínamo and Emol each report the hospital's own statement on the incident; the statement itself was not read directly. Neither says whether data was accessed.

review.note: Title gave the hospital the cyberattack label, but it only said systems were affected; title now attributes it to Emol; status confirmed to developing
